title: SLA playbook for priority lanes with hysteresis and probing
creator: Samira Patel
description:
Summary: Define an operational SLA and rollout playbook for 'priority lanes' — a per-tenant prioritization feature that routes high-tier customers to lower-latency pools. The PRD clarifies latency envelopes, uptime guarantees, error-budget accounting rules, and progressive rollback/mitigation actions. The goal is to allow safe, measurable rollouts of priority lanes while protecting overall platform SLOs and avoiding oscillation via hysteresis and active probing.

Scope: This ticket covers the product-level SLA definition, acceptance criteria, staged rollout gates, and handoff requirements for Engineering (implementation of throttles, routing, hysteresis) and Observability (dashboards, probes, alerts). It does NOT cover the implementation of tenant billing changes or legal SLA contract language (those will be separate).

Out-of-scope: pricing changes, contract signatures, per-tenant legal addenda, per-region capacity procurement decisions.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Latency targets defined per priority tier and workload class: p50/p95/p99 for interactive chat and p95/p99 for embeddings.
2) Uptime target: 99.95% per-month for priority lanes; degradation actions defined when monthly error budget consumption reaches 20%, 50%, 80%.
3) Error budget calc: per-tenant weighted by traffic volume and priority tier; documented formula and example calculations included.
4) Hysteresis rules: clear thresholds and hold windows to prevent rapid flip-flop (example: if a priority lane falls below p95 target for 3 consecutive 5-min probes, enter mitigation; only re-enable after 30m stable).
5) Canary/probe plan: canary traffic percent schedule, probe queries, synthetic session continuity tests, and manual/automated rollback triggers.
6) Monitoring: dashboards and alerting playbooks for burn-rate, tail latency, request success rate, and routing health.
7) Runbook: scripted mitigation steps at each error budget threshold (throttle, degrade to fallback model, expand capacity, notify stakeholders).
8) QA: Integration tests and chaos probes run against staging that simulate 2x normal load and measure hysteresis behavior.
9) Docs: Confluence PRD and Console UX copy for tenant config surfaced to support and SRE.
decisions:
- Use tenant-weighted error-budget formula (weighted by request count and priority multiplier) instead of flat per-tenant budgets to avoid punishing high-volume tenants.
- Hysteresis window set to 30 minutes stable before re-enabling a lane; probe cadence 5 minutes.
- Canary rollout will proceed in 3 waves: 1% of eligible priority traffic -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%, with evaluation windows at each stage.
- Automated rollback triggers on sustained >50% burn rate over 1 hour or p99 exceeding target by >50% for 15 min.
scope_changes:
- After stakeholder review (2025-02-20) we narrowed initial launch to hosted & dedicated control-plane routing (exclude on-prem private deployment until hysteresis patterns are validated).
- Added explicit requirement for synthetic session continuity probes following a recent incident where tail latency persisted after partial capacity restoration.
rollout_gates:
Gate 0: Documentation & PRD complete; test plan reviewed by SRE and PM.
Gate 1 (Canary start): 1% traffic with synthetic probes passing for 24h and burn rate <20%.
Gate 2: 10% traffic with production load tests and observed hysteresis behavior for 48h; burn rate <30%.
Gate 3: 50% traffic with capacity autoscale exercised and all alerts green for 72h.
Gate 4: Full rollout with post-launch monitoring for 7 days and follow-up retrospective.
Emergency gate: any sustained p99 > 2x target for 15 minutes or >80% error-budget consumption triggers automatic rollback and incident bridge.
monitoring_and_metrics:
Required metrics (names to be instrumented in telemetry):
- priority_lane.request_count (by tenant, tier)
- priority_lane.success_rate (per minute)
- priority_lane.latency_p50/p95/p99 (per workload class)
- priority_lane.error_budget_remaining (per tenant)
- priority_lane.burn_rate (1h rolling)
- routing.degradation_actions.count
- probe.synthetic_session_success_rate
Dashboards: pre-made dashboard links (staging and prod) will be created; alert thresholds enumerated in the runbook.
test_plan:
1) Unit tests for weighted error-budget calculation with edge cases.
2) Integration tests: simulate noisy neighbor scenarios and ensure hysteresis prevents flip-flop.
3) Load test: 2x expected peak with priority lane routes enabled; record latency envelopes.
4) Chaos test: randomly kill a fraction of priority pool replicas and verify automated mitigation engages and recovers per playbook.
5) Canary validation: run synthetic probes and validate runbook triggers for Tier A tenants.
